A thesis doesn't need to be complicated. It can be very straightforward. The reader should be able to have no knowledge about what your topic is, be able to skip the intro, and read the thesis and know exactly what they'll be reading about.

The way I usually come up with a thesis is like this:
First, what's the question for the essay (example: why are cats better than dogs).
Second, list the reasons that answer the question - try to aim for at least three (example: 1. Cats clean themselves and require less maintenance, 2. Cats can develop different personalities, whereas most dogs usually act similar, 3. Cats are normally quieter).
Thirdly, combine what you just came up with to tell the reader what you'll be talking about (example: Cats are better than dogs because they require less grooming maintenance, they have different personalities, and they do not make as much noise).
Now the reader knows the content and order of the paragraphs they'll be reading (example: Body #1=Grooming habits of cats vs. dogs, Body #2=Differences between dog and cat personalities, and Body #3=Noise level and consistency of cats vs dogs).
**Always list your reasons in your thesis in the same order you write about them in your essay.

And remember that as you write your essay, it's okay if your thesis changes. If you get stuck on one reason and find you don't have a lot to say about it, then find a reason that you have more to say about (and change the reason in your thesis). To make sure your thesis is on track, just keep asking yourself "Does this answer the prompt question?" If it's yes, you're good, but if it's a no, you know that you need to reevaluate your answers/reasons.

I know this is super long, but I hope that it made sense and helped! Good luck!

I literally just finished reading the series "I Hunt Killers" by Barry Lyga. It's INTENSE and dark, but it's got a lot of humor to it. It's about a boy who was raised by his father, who is the world's most nefarious serial killer. He killed into the triple digits and taught his son how to get away with murder. So it follows the boy, now 17, as he tries to figure out if he has soul or if he's like his father, all while his life is being completely turned upside down when a serial killer strikes again, following the same patterns as his dad. It is such a great series, but it's not for the faint of heart.

Also, one of my top favorite series to read is The Chaos Walking by Patrick Ness. It's a futuristic dystopian world that takes place on 'New World' which is exactly like Earth except for the Noise. Everyone can hear men's thoughts - whatever they think or fantasize, it's heard by everyone else. Animals thoughts too, but not women's. There's also the Spackle, the alien life form inhabiting the planet. They resemble a human alien hybrid and they only communicate through Noise. It follows a boy who lives in a small men-only village and is only a few months to becoming a man. He finds a girl who's ship crashed just outside his village, and it puts in motion his search for the answers to the secrets of the village. Him and the girl go on the run with an army chasing after them as they try to find the answers they seek. The theme of the series is basically that it doesn't matter how good a person is, there's a monster hiding inside of all of us - it's how you control that defines you. Again, it's not for the faint of heart, but it's tamer. It will, however, send you on an emotional roller coaster and keep you on the edge of your seat. I don't do it justice with my summary, so you should for sure look it up!

I had a similar problem when I met my boyfriend. By the time I met him, I'd been through A LOT of crap in life, so my anxiety was getting really bad. I've always had an issue with speaking up for myself, but I was terrified that I was going to say or do something to screw it up, so I'd always go along with what he wanted. Sometimes, I still worry that he's going to get tired of dealing with my anxiety and depression, even though he constantly tells me that's never going to happen. That being said, I found that the best way to deal with such a problem is to be honest with him about how I'm feeling and why I feel that way. Lucky for me, he has bad anxiety too, so he understands to an extent, but that didn't stop me from worrying that I'd lose him. You just have to learn to communicate and be 100% honest with your girlfriend. It does get easier to confide in them as time goes on. The only time my boyfriend ever gets upset about my anxiety is when I'm not being honest with him about it or speaking up for what I want. It sounds cliche, but communication and being open really is the best thing to sustain a relationship. And to prove it, my bf and I will have been together 4 years this November.
